tools.name: init_book_repo
tools.description: Create the local Narrarium repository structure for a book project, including folders, guidelines, summaries, evaluations, and reusable skills.

tools.name: setup_framework
tools.description:
Return the exact npx commands and setup steps to bootstrap a new Narrarium project from scratch, or to upgrade an existing book repo.

Use this tool when the user asks how to set up the framework, how to upgrade, or how to install Narrarium.

## Creating a new book
Run from any empty folder:
```
npx create-narrarium-book . --title "My Book" --language en --author "Author Name"
```
Answer **y** when npx asks to install the package.
Add `--with-reader` to also scaffold the Astro reader site.

## Upgrading an existing book repo
Run from the **book root** (the folder that contains `book.md`):
```
npx create-narrarium-book . --upgrade
```
Answer **y** when npx asks to install the package.
To also upgrade the reader scaffold, add `--with-reader`.
After the upgrade, install reader dependencies:
```
cd reader
npm install
```

## Notes
- The workflow file `.github/workflows/deploy-reader-pages.yml` is **never overwritten** on upgrade — your password secret and any manual edits are preserved.
- The MCP server config (`.vscode/mcp.json`, `opencode.jsonc`) is also never overwritten.
- Reader personas are seeded automatically on first create or upgrade if the `personas/` folder is empty.

tools.name: chapter_writing_context
tools.description: Assemble the point-in-time context that should be read before writing or polishing a chapter: prose defaults, scoped story-so-far context, prior chapter state, and matching chapter draft without leaking later story material. In prose, keep canon names as plain text instead of markdown links; the reader resolves visible mentions.

tools.name: paragraph_writing_context
tools.description: Assemble the point-in-time context that should be read before writing or polishing a paragraph: prose defaults, scoped story-so-far context, prior scenes only, and the matching paragraph draft or final paragraph without leaking later story material. In prose, keep canon names as plain text instead of markdown links; the reader resolves visible mentions.

tools.name: revise_chapter
tools.description: Propose a chapter-level editorial pass without writing files. Use this when you want diagnosis plus scene-by-scene rewrite proposals for an existing final chapter. The result can also suggest merged state_changes review if multiple scenes touch continuity-sensitive beats.

tools.name: revise_paragraph
tools.description: Propose a revision for an existing final paragraph without writing files. Use this for targeted editorial passes like clarity, pacing, tension, dialogue, voice, show-dont-tell, or redundancy cleanup. Show the proposal to the user first, then apply it with update_paragraph only after clear confirmation. The result can also suggest state_changes to review if the paragraph carries continuity-sensitive beats.

tools.name: review_dialogue_action_beats
tools.description: Review a final paragraph beat by beat to judge whether dialogue-adjacent actions are purposeful, weak, or better replaced with a simple speech tag. This is proposal-only and may also suggest new beats or recurring tics worth observing for character canon.

tools.name: resume_book_context
tools.description: Assemble restart context for a book project using prose rules, stable context, summaries, and exported conversations. You can also scope it to a target chapter or paragraph so the canon only reflects the story up to that writing point.

tools.name: create_entity
tools.description: Create a canonical entity markdown file inside the local book repository. Use this for quick stubs, items, locations, factions, secrets, and timeline events. Prefer create_character for full story characters.

tools.name: create_chapter
tools.description: Create a chapter folder, chapter metadata file, and paired resume and evaluation files in the local book repository. In prose bodies, keep canon names as plain text instead of markdown links to canon files.

tools.name: create_paragraph
tools.description: Create a numbered paragraph or scene markdown file inside an existing chapter folder. In prose bodies, keep canon names as plain text instead of markdown links to canon files.

tools.name: create_chapter_draft
tools.description: Create a rough chapter draft inside drafts/ using the same chapter slug structure as the final chapter tree. Keep canon names as plain text in the draft prose instead of markdown links.

tools.name: update_chapter_draft
tools.description: Update an existing chapter draft by patching its frontmatter and replacing or appending rough draft body content.

tools.name: update_book_notes
tools.description: Update the global working notes or story-design document. Use appendBody when the user asks you to keep a note without replacing the whole file.

tools.name: save_book_item
tools.description: Create or update a structured idea or note entry at book level. Use this for active idea queues and note queues rather than freeform body edits.

tools.name: save_chapter_item
tools.description: Create or update a structured idea or note entry tied to a chapter draft.

tools.name: update_chapter_notes
tools.description: Update or append chapter-specific working notes stored in drafts/<chapter>/notes.md. Use this when the user wants to keep or refine notes tied to a chapter draft.

tools.name: promote_book_item
tools.description: Promote a structured book-level idea or note out of the active queue. You can move it into notes or story design, or archive it as promoted after you already used it in a draft.

tools.name: promote_chapter_item
tools.description: Promote a structured chapter-level idea or note out of the active queue. You can move it into chapter notes or archive it as promoted after using it in draft work.

tools.name: create_paragraph_draft
tools.description: Create a rough paragraph or scene draft inside drafts/ using the same chapter tree as the final chapter.

tools.name: update_paragraph_draft
tools.description: Update an existing paragraph draft by patching its frontmatter and replacing or appending rough scene content. Keep canon names as plain text in the draft prose instead of markdown links.

tools.name: create_chapter_from_draft
tools.description: Promote a chapter draft into the final chapters/ tree. It copies structural frontmatter from drafts/, accepts polished body text if provided, and syncs plot.md after writing. Final prose should keep canon names as plain text instead of markdown links.

tools.name: create_paragraph_from_draft
tools.description: Promote a paragraph draft into the final chapters/ tree. It copies structural frontmatter from drafts/, accepts polished body text if provided, and syncs plot.md after writing. Final prose should keep canon names as plain text instead of markdown links.

tools.name: generate_asset_image
tools.description: Generate an image for a canonical subject, save it into the assets tree, and keep the asset prompt metadata in sync.

tools.name: update_chapter
tools.description: Update an existing chapter metadata file and optional chapter notes body. Use this for summary, POV, tags, and chapter notes changes without touching chapter numbering or folder naming. In prose bodies, keep canon names as plain text instead of markdown links.

tools.name: update_paragraph
tools.description: Apply an existing paragraph or scene revision after the user confirmed it. Use this for summary, viewpoint, tags, and body revisions without renumbering or renaming the file. Keep canon names as plain text instead of markdown links; the MCP layer refreshes plot and resume files after the update.

tools.name: apply_dialogue_action_beats

tools.name: evaluate_chapter
tools.description: Refresh a full chapter evaluation by reading the whole chapter across all paragraph files, combining objective text signals with editorial reading against the active writing-style files and canon coherence checks, then writing objective/editorial scores, a weighted verdict, an explanation of why that verdict landed there, and next steps plus paragraph evaluation files.

tools.name: evaluate_paragraph
tools.description: Refresh the saved evaluation for a single paragraph while still using the full chapter as context, including objective scores, writing-style-aware editorial notes, canon coherence checks, a weighted verdict, an explanation of why that verdict landed there, and concrete next steps.

tools.name: prepare_paragraph_evaluation
tools.description: Compute objective text metrics and style context for a single paragraph and return them as structured data so the LLM can perform the editorial reading before calling write_paragraph_evaluation. Call this first, read the result carefully, then call write_paragraph_evaluation with your editorial judgment.

tools.name: write_paragraph_evaluation
tools.description: Write the final paragraph evaluation file using LLM-supplied editorial strengths, concerns, canon notes, next steps, and verdict explanation combined with objective metrics recomputed from the current chapter state. Call prepare_paragraph_evaluation first to obtain the objective data before calling this tool.

editorialStrengths.description: 1–4 specific editorial strengths observed in the prose

canonStrengths.description: 0–3 ways the paragraph handles canon mentions well

nextSteps.description: 1–4 concrete revision actions for this paragraph

verdictExplanation.description: 2–4 sentences explaining why the combined score lands where it does

tools.name: evaluate_book
tools.description: Refresh the total book evaluation with chapter scorecards, writing-style-aware editorial checks, canon coherence checks, weighted verdict summaries, explicit verdict explanations, and revision priorities, and optionally refresh all chapter and paragraph evaluations too.

tools.name: wikipedia_search
tools.description: Search English and the user's request language Wikipedia for historical or factual research before adding canon to the book repository.

tools.name: wikipedia_page
tools.description: Fetch English and the user's request language Wikipedia page summaries and save them into research/wikipedia inside the local book repository.

tools.name: export_epub
tools.description: Export the current book repository into an EPUB file from the ordered chapter and paragraph markdown files.

tools.name: create_persona
tools.description:
Create a reader persona file in personas/ of the book repository.
Personas represent fictional reader archetypes used to review chapters from different perspectives.
Each persona has reading habits, values, dislikes, beauty and readability focus areas, emotional triggers, and tolerance scores.
Use seed_default_personas to populate the book with the five built-in archetypes instead of creating one manually.

rootPath.description: Absolute path to the book repository root

name.description: Full display name of the persona, e.g. 'The Casual Reader'

archetype.description: Short archetype label, e.g. 'casual reader', 'literary critic'

slug.description: File slug (auto-derived from name if omitted)

readingHabits.description: How and why this persona reads

values.description: What this persona values most in a story

dislikes.description: What this persona dislikes or finds off-putting

beautyFocus.description: Aspects this persona focuses on when judging prose beauty

readabilityFocus.description: Aspects this persona focuses on when judging readability

complexityTolerance.description: Tolerance for narrative complexity (1=very low, 5=very high)

pacingTolerance.description: Tolerance for slow pacing (1=very low, 5=very high)

body.description: Optional custom markdown body; auto-generated if omitted

tools.name: seed_default_personas
tools.description:
Seed the book repository with the five built-in reader personas if they do not already exist.
The default personas are: The Casual Reader, The Literary Critic, The Genre Fan, The Empathetic Reader, The Impatient Skimmer.
Already-existing persona files are never overwritten.
Call this once when setting up a new book to have a ready-made panel of reviewers.

rootPath.description: Absolute path to the book repository root

tools.name: list_personas
tools.description:
List all reader personas defined in the book repository's personas/ folder.
Returns each persona's slug, name, archetype, complexity tolerance, and pacing tolerance.
Use this before calling review_chapter_with_personas to know which personas are available.

rootPath.description: Absolute path to the book repository root

tools.name: review_chapter_with_personas
tools.description:
Review a chapter from the perspective of one or more reader personas and write the results to evaluations/chapters/<chapter>/personas-review.md.

## Workflow
1. Call list_personas (or load the persona files directly) to know which personas exist.
2. Read the chapter prose using chapter_writing_context or by reading the chapter files directly.
3. For each persona, simulate how that reader would experience the chapter:
   - Assign a beauty score (1–10): how aesthetically pleasing is the prose to this persona?
   - Assign a readability score (1–10): how easy and enjoyable is it to read for this persona?
   - Write an overall impression (2–4 sentences in the persona's voice).
   - List 2–4 strengths (what worked for this persona).
   - List 2–4 concerns (what didn't work or felt off).
   - List 1–3 concrete suggestions from this persona's point of view.
4. Pass all reviews to this tool — it writes the consolidated personas-review.md file.

The file is placed alongside the editorial evaluation in evaluations/chapters/<chapter>/personas-review.md.

rootPath.description: Absolute path to the book repository root

chapterSlug.description: Slug of the chapter being reviewed

overallImpression.description: 2–4 sentence overall impression in the persona's voice

strengths.description: 2–4 things that worked for this persona

tools.name: create_script
tools.description:
Create a new scene script in scripts/<chapter>/<paragraph>.md using the Narrarium script meta-language.

## Script meta-language legend

| Syntax       | Meaning                                                         |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Location:`  | Where the scene takes place (free text or canon location slug)  |
| `[...]`      | **Tell beat** — quick narrative summary, shown not shown        |
| `{...}`      | **Emotion/state beat** — character feeling or internal event    |
| `(...)`      | **Action beat** — physical action performed by a character      |
| `«...»`      | **Dialogue idea** — what a character should say (not verbatim)  |
| `#...`       | **Author comment** — thematic note or reminder, not prose       |

Rules:
- One beat per line.
- Beats are ordered as they should appear in the final prose.
- `Location:` must be the first line if present.
- `#` comments are never rendered into prose — they are instructions to the writer.
- Multiple beats of the same type can appear in any order.

## When to use
- Before writing a paragraph from scratch: write the script first, then call `script_to_paragraph`.
- When the user wants to plan a scene without committing to final prose.
- When the user dictates a scene in shorthand and you need to store it.

The script file mirrors the chapter/paragraph structure of chapters/ and drafts/.
File path: `scripts/<chapter-slug>/<paragraph-slug>.md`

rootPath.description: Absolute path to the book repository root

title.description: Paragraph title (used to build the filename slug)

location.description: Where the scene takes place — free text or canon location slug

body.description: Full script body using the meta-language. If omitted a template is generated.

overwrite.description: Overwrite if the script already exists

tools.name: update_script
tools.description:
Update an existing scene script in scripts/<chapter>/<paragraph>.md.

Use this to refine beats, add new lines, or patch frontmatter (e.g. change location or tags).
Provide `body` to fully replace the script body, or `appendBody` to add lines at the end.

## Script meta-language legend

| Syntax       | Meaning                                                         |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Location:`  | Where the scene takes place (free text or canon location slug)  |
| `[...]`      | **Tell beat** — quick narrative summary, shown not shown        |
| `{...}`      | **Emotion/state beat** — character feeling or internal event    |
| `(...)`      | **Action beat** — physical action performed by a character      |
| `«...»`      | **Dialogue idea** — what a character should say (not verbatim)  |
| `#...`       | **Author comment** — thematic note or reminder, not prose       |

Rules:
- One beat per line.
- Beats are ordered as they should appear in the final prose.
- `Location:` must be the first line if present.
- `#` comments are never rendered into prose — they are instructions to the writer.
- Multiple beats of the same type can appear in any order.

rootPath.description: Absolute path to the book repository root

body.description: New full script body — replaces existing content

appendBody.description: Lines to append to the existing script body

frontmatterPatch.description: Frontmatter fields to patch (e.g. location, tags)

tools.name: read_script
tools.description:
Read an existing scene script and return its meta-language body plus the legend.

Use this to inspect a script before writing prose, or to check what beats are planned.

rootPath.description: Absolute path to the book repository root

tools.name: script_to_paragraph
tools.description:
Assemble the full writing context needed to turn a scene script into polished prose.

Returns:
- The script body with meta-language beats
- The script meta-language legend
- The book writing-style guideline
- The existing paragraph body if one already exists (revision mode)

After calling this tool, write the paragraph prose following the writing-style rules and the beat order in the script, then call `create_paragraph` or `update_paragraph` with the result.

rootPath.description: Absolute path to the book repository root

tools.name: paragraph_to_script
tools.description:
Reverse-engineer a scene script skeleton from an existing paragraph body.

Use this when:
- A paragraph was written without a script and you want to create one retroactively.
- You want to analyse the structure of an existing scene.
- You want to create a script template that mirrors what was already written.

The tool returns a suggested script body. Review and refine it, then call `create_script` or `update_script` to save it.

rootPath.description: Absolute path to the book repository root
